questions.q: What does a low-interaction honeypot actually run behind its convincing banner or login prompt?
options: A full copy of the production system it's imitating
A live connection directly into the internal network
Nothing real — it's a minimal simulation with no real service or shell underneath
A real database containing fake customer records
questions.explain: Low-interaction honeypots simulate a service minimally, logging probes and login attempts without any real system behind them.

questions.q: What is the real tradeoff of a high-interaction honeypot compared to a low-interaction one?
options: Lower cost to deploy, but it can never log any attacker activity at all
Far richer attacker intelligence, but higher operational risk if it isn't properly isolated
It can only be used to detect attacks against web applications
It requires no maintenance once deployed, unlike low-interaction honeypots
questions.explain: A high-interaction honeypot is a real, fully-functional system, so it yields deeper intelligence but must be isolated to contain real risk.

questions.q: In the SSH honeypot example, why does the attacker's login attempt go nowhere even if they guess a valid-looking username and password?
options: Because there is no real SSH daemon or shell behind the emulated banner
Because low-interaction honeypots require multi-factor authentication
Because the attacker's IP address gets permanently blocked
Because the honeypot immediately alerts law enforcement
questions.explain: The honeypot only presents a convincing banner and logs the attempt — there is no real system underneath for the attacker to reach.

questions.q: Why must a high-interaction honeypot be rigorously isolated and segmented from the real network?
options: Because high-interaction honeypots are illegal to run without isolation
Because isolation prevents the honeypot from logging any attacker activity
Because an attacker who gains real access to it could otherwise use it as a launching point elsewhere
Because isolation is what makes the honeypot look convincing to attackers
questions.explain: Without isolation, a high-interaction honeypot stops being a safe intelligence tool and becomes an actual foothold for the attacker.

questions.q: Why do most real deception strategies deploy both low- and high-interaction honeypots?
options: High-interaction honeypots are being phased out in favor of low-interaction ones entirely
They serve identical purposes, so using both is purely redundant
Low-interaction ones act as cheap, broad tripwires, while high-interaction ones give deep intelligence on specific attackers
Low-interaction honeypots are required by law in most industries
questions.explain: Low-interaction honeypots give broad, cheap coverage, while high-interaction honeypots are reserved for deeper, riskier intelligence gathering.
